rich_summary: This section depicts the terrifying night battle between the Rakshasa prince Ghatotkacha, son of Bhima, and the Kaurava forces led by Karna. After Ghatotkacha slays the Rakshasa ally Alayudha and throws his severed head before Duryodhana, panic spreads among the Kauravas. Karna enters the fray and clashes with Ghatotkacha in a spectacular duel marked by torrents of arrows and supernatural illusions. Ghatotkacha unleashes devastating magical assaults—clouds raining weapons, rocks, and thunderbolts—throwing the Kaurava army into chaos. As the army nears destruction, the Kauravas beg Karna to use the divine spear granted by Indra, a weapon he had reserved to kill Arjuna. Forced by desperation, Karna hurls the irresistible dart at Ghatotkacha, a momentous decision that saves the Kauravas but sacrifices his best chance to defeat Arjuna later.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the supernatural tone of the battle as Alayudha and Ghatotkacha unleash illusions that transform the battlefield into a storm‑like spectacle.
Describes the ferocious close combat culminating in Ghatotkacha seizing and beheading Alayudha, a pivotal victory that lifts Pandava morale.
The vivid metaphor comparing the night battle to a thundercloud—bows as lightning and arrows as rain—captures the epic scale and poetic imagery of the war.
Depicts the terror caused by Ghatotkacha’s illusion: raining weapons, monstrous apparitions, and panicked soldiers, emphasizing the psychological devastation of the Kaurava army.
The crucial moment when Karna resolves to use Indra’s divine dart—originally reserved for Arjuna—marking a strategic turning point in the epic.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ghatotkacha and Alayudha hurl mountains, trees, and storms of weapons at each other beneath a sky blackened with supernatural clouds and lightning.
Ghatotkacha stands roaring over the battlefield, holding the severed head of Alayudha before the Pandava army as drums and conches thunder through the night.
Karna, surrounded by fleeing Kaurava troops and a sky raining weapons from Ghatotkacha’s illusion, raises the blazing divine dart of Indra to strike the giant Rakshasa.
